Assign Dominant Annotation to Neighbourhoods

Source: R/nhood_annotation.R
nhood_annotation.Rd

Computes per-neighbourhood the proportion of cells belonging to each category of one or more annotation columns and assigns a dominant identity based on a user-defined threshold. Neighbourhoods where no single category exceeds the threshold are labelled "mixed".

Usage

nhood_annotation(
  object,
  nhood_col = NULL,
  annotation_cols = "celltype",
  threshold = 0.7,
  result_name = "nhood_annotation"
)

Arguments

object

A Milo or SingleCellExperiment object. Seurat objects must first be converted via as.SingleCellExperiment.

nhood_col

Character string. For plain SingleCellExperiment objects (i.e. not Milo), the name of the colData column containing neighbourhood assignments. Not required for Milo objects.

annotation_cols

Character vector of colData column names containing per-cell annotation categories to summarise per neighbourhood (e.g. cell type, lineage, cluster label). All specified columns must be present in colData; missing columns raise an error. Default: "celltype".

threshold

Numeric value between 0-1. The minimum proportion a single annotation category must reach for a neighbourhood to be assigned that label. Neighbourhoods where the dominant category falls below this threshold are assigned "mixed". Default: 0.7.

result_name

Character string. Key under which the results data.frame is stored in metadata(object). If an entry with this name already exists a warning is emitted and the entry is overwritten. Default: "nhood_annotation".

Value

The input object, with a data.frame stored in metadata(object)[[result_name]]. The data.frame has one row per neighbourhood and the following columns:

nhood

Neighbourhood identifier.

nhood_size

Total number of cells in the neighbourhood.

<annotation_col>

Dominant annotation label for this neighbourhood, or "mixed" if no single category reached threshold. One column per entry in annotation_cols.

<annotation_col>_dominant_prop

Proportion of cells carrying the dominant annotation label. One column per entry in annotation_cols.

Details

Object type handling

  • Milo objects: Neighbourhood membership is read directly from the sparse nhoods matrix via nhoods. Row names of this matrix must match colnames(object); a mismatch raises an error to prevent silent misassignment.

  • Plain SingleCellExperiment objects: A binary neighbourhood membership matrix is constructed internally from the column specified by nhood_col. Cells with NA assignments are excluded with a warning.

Dominant label assignment

Each neighbourhood represents a group of transcriptionally similar cells. For each neighbourhood and each annotation column, per-cell labels are tabulated and converted to proportions. The category with the highest proportion is the candidate dominant label. If that proportion is >= threshold the neighbourhood is assigned that label; otherwise it is labelled "mixed", indicating that no single annotation category predominates. When multiple annotation columns are supplied the procedure is applied independently for each.

See also

nhood_annotation_props, nhood_diversity, nhood_shm, nhood_cdr3_convergence

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# --- Milo object, single annotation column --------------------------------
milo <- nhood_annotation(
  object          = milo_object,
  annotation_cols = "celltype",
  threshold       = 0.7
)
results <- S4Vectors::metadata(milo)[["nhood_annotation"]]

# --- Multiple annotation columns, relaxed threshold ----------------------
milo <- nhood_annotation(
  object          = milo_object,
  annotation_cols = c("celltype", "lineage"),
  threshold       = 0.6,
  result_name     = "nhood_annotation"
)

# --- Plain SingleCellExperiment object ------------------------------------
sce <- nhood_annotation(
  object          = sce_object,
  nhood_col       = "community_id",
  annotation_cols = "celltype"
)
} # }
